summary: Satoru Harada specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). His career includes positions at the Toyo Bunko, the Eastern Institute, and as a professor at Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies, having studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
Satoshi Fujiwara is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Satoshi Hayashima focuses on Buddhist studies. He was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served there as a lecturer (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Gregory Schopen, he held posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Satoshi Ito works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a professor at Ibaraki University (attested 2007).
Satoshi Kono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he also served as an assistant professor (attested 2016–2020).

Satya Narayan Goenka was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin (~1955–1969). In 1985, he founded the Vipassana Research Institute and taught numerous prominent students.

Satya Swarup Misra is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satya Vrat Shastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of the Punjab, Banaras Hindu University, and Punjabi University under Charu Deva Shastri, Shukdev Jha, and Siddheshwar Varma. He served at the University of Delhi and held multiple visiting professorships.

Satyanad Kichenassamy studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Pierre and Marie Curie University. He held positions at the Courant Institute, the University of Minnesota, the University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne (1998), and Paris Sciences et Lettres University (2023–2026).

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka, and later served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Saurabh Singh works in archaeology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from the University of Delhi, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, and Deccan College. He served as Principal Investigator at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2022–2023) and Adjunct Assistant Professor at Delhi (2024).

Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded the Panditarama Meditation Center, serving as its abbot.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied under U Paññāvanta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at University College, Colombo. In Buddhist studies, he held leadership roles at several monasteries, served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999), and founded Dhammānanda Vihara.

Sayadaw U Thittila was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1933–1934). He served as librarian at the Buddhist Society and Adyar Library, and as Lecturer in Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Rangoon (1952).

Sayagyi U Ba Khin was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Saya Thetgyi (~1937–1945). He founded the International Meditation Centre and taught disciples including Satya Narayan Goenka and Mother Sayamagyi.

Sayaka Sonoda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at Toyo University under Shinobu Yamaguchi and Shogo Watanabe. In 2020, she held posts at the Cabinet Office and as a visiting researcher at Toyo University.
Sayori Tsubota is an Indology scholar who conducted doctoral studies at Osaka University (attested 2020). She holds a post as a JSPS postdoctoral fellow at Tohoku University (attested 2026).
